clue.text: Reportedly voracious reader?

indicators.note: reportedly means the word we want is only heard, so a name that sounds the same is spoken here

parts.note: Hannibal Lecter, the cannibal of Thomas Harris's novels, has a voracious appetite for people

explanation.surface: A rumour about someone who devours books.
explanation.walkthrough: The '?' flags the joke: 'voracious reader' sounds like a bookworm, but the voracious one is the fictional man-eater Hannibal Lecter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lector is a reader, especially one who reads lessons in church or lectures at a university.

clue.text: Imprinted flower-girl in Irish play

parts.note: the Cockney flower-seller of Shaw's Pygmalion, a character who exists in print

explanation.surface: A flower-seller in a Shaw drama.
explanation.walkthrough: Shaw was Irish; in Pygmalion the flower-girl Doolittle is taught to speak like a duchess.
explanation.definitionFit: Doolittle is the flower-seller heroine of Pygmalion, by the Irish playwright Shaw.

clue.text: Irish play providing its own first-nighter

definitions.text: Irish play providing its own first-nighter

parts.words: Irish play providing its own first-nighter
parts.note: a Sheridan comedy whose title names the reviewer who attends opening performances

explanation.surface: A play that brings along its own reviewer.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheridan was born in Dublin; a first-nighter is someone at an opening performance, typically a reviewer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheridan's 1779 burlesque is titled after the reviewer who goes to opening nights.

clue.text: Duchess of Cornwall conceals a world-stage actor manager

indicators.note: conceals means the duchess's name holds the next piece tucked inside it

parts.note: in King Lear, Regan is married to the Duke of Cornwall

explanation.surface: A royal duchess hides an international theatre impresario.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duchess of Cornwall suggests modern royalty, but she is Lear's daughter Regan. 'world-stage actor manager' is a film actor who went on to run the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald Reagan was a Hollywood actor before he became US president, managing affairs on the world stage.

clue.text: Old Christmas tree a present from Norway

definitions.text: Old Christmas tree a present from Norway

parts.words: Old Christmas tree a present from Norway
parts.note: the great ash of Norse myth, playfully cast as an ancient version of the fir Norway gives London each Christmas

explanation.surface: The annual Norwegian gift of a Christmas tree to London.
explanation.walkthrough: Norway sends a tree to Trafalgar Square every Christmas; the clue points instead to the world tree of Norse mythology.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse mythology the cosmic ash tree binds the nine worlds together, a very old tree from Scandinavia.

clue.text: Irish play providing warning to Swiss marksman?

definitions.meaning: a comedy by the Dublin-born Shaw
a caution addressed to William Tell, the legendary Swiss archer

explanation.surface: A drama that cautions a Swiss sharpshooter.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw wrote a comedy with this title, and the phrase also reads as advice to the archer Tell.

clue.text: His son made a name as a high-flier

definitions.text: His son made a name as a high-flier

parts.words: His son made a name as a high-flier
parts.note: the boy Icarus flew too near the sun on wings his father built

explanation.surface: A proud father whose boy became a high achiever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flier' suggests a successful career, but Icarus literally flew; the Icarian Sea is named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical craftsman made wax wings for his son Icarus, who flew too high and fell.

clue.text: Some heat hostilities engender for swordsman

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Fierce fighting breeds a fencer.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'engender for', but those are link words; the definition is 'swordsman', one of Dumas's Three Musketeers.
explanation.definitionFit: He is one of Dumas's Three Musketeers, famed for fighting with the blade.

clue.text: Bride's response to chaps (English and American) suitable for Cretan king

parts.note: a bride answers 'I do' at the altar
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A bride's wedding vow to suitable men from both sides of the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: He was a king of Crete who led its forces at Troy, and the hero of Mozart's opera.

clue.text: Sort of true retail reading matter

indicators.note: sort here means arrange, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A kind of honest shopkeeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Books and writing in general are what people read.

clue.text: Gangster poet?

explanation.surface: A criminal who writes verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoodlum is a gangster, and Thomas Hood wrote 'The Song of the Shirt'.

clue.text: Gilbert spoke of a steamer like a very small second-class one

definitions.text: Gilbert spoke of a steamer like a very small second-class one

parts.words: Gilbert spoke of a steamer like a very small second-class one
parts.note: W. S. Gilbert compared a cramped boat to a tiny railway compartment of the lower class

explanation.surface: W. S. Gilbert describing a cramped little ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Second-class here is railway travel: Gilbert likened the steamer to a small railway vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway passenger coach, divided into classes, is the comparison Gilbert drew.

clue.text: He offered a lesson for fathers

definitions.text: He offered a lesson for fathers

parts.words: He offered a lesson for fathers
parts.note: the pen-name of Thomas Guthrie, whose novel Vice Versa was subtitled A Lesson to Fathers

explanation.surface: A man giving advice on parenting.
explanation.walkthrough: Vice Versa (1882) has a father and son swap bodies; its subtitle is 'A Lesson to Fathers'.
explanation.definitionFit: F. was the pen-name initial of the Victorian author who wrote Vice Versa, a comic lesson for parents.

clue.text: Tax Linklater, for example

definitions.meaning: an old word for a levy
Eric Linklater was a novelist from Scotland

explanation.surface: Taxing the novelist Linklater.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval levy shares the word with a native of Scotland, like Eric Linklater.

clue.text: Novelist truly harbouring vehicle

indicators.note: harbouring means the first word shelters the second inside it

parts.note: certes is an archaic word for truly
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A writer who honestly keeps a car.
explanation.walkthrough: CERTES is old-fashioned English for 'certainly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish author wrote Don Quixote, the great early novel.

clue.text: What Frédéric Moreau became, sentimentally

parts.note: Moreau is the hero of Flaubert's Sentimental Education

explanation.surface: How a French character developed emotionally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentimentally' points to Flaubert's L'Education sentimentale, whose hero Moreau undergoes that schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaubert's novel is the Sentimental Education, so its hero ends up schooled.

clue.text: Old healer is upscale, anyway

indicators.note: anyway means in any manner, so these letters may be set in any order

explanation.surface: An ancient doctor who is upmarket regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the Greek god of medicine, whose snake-entwined staff is still a symbol of doctors.

clue.text: She carried considerable weight in ancient Greece

definitions.text: She carried considerable weight in ancient Greece

parts.words: She carried considerable weight in ancient Greece
parts.note: a carved female figure holding up a temple roof, like those of the Erechtheion

explanation.surface: An influential woman in classical Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carried considerable weight' sounds like influence, but she literally supports a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A sculpted woman used as a column bears the entablature of a Greek temple.

clue.text: Like Longfellow's Psalm of Life

parts.note: the poem's metre: stressed then unstressed syllables, 'Tell me not in mournful numbers'

explanation.surface: Resembling a well-known Longfellow poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A Psalm of Life is written in feet of a long syllable followed by a short one.

clue.text: Throw actors together

definitions.meaning: the full company of performers in a production

explanation.surface: Tossing performers into a group.
explanation.definitionFit: To fling something is one sense; the whole company of performers in a play is the other.

clue.text: Measure ring for version of Shakespeare

parts.note: a quart is a measure of liquid
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A ring measured up for a Shakespeare edition.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's plays first appeared in small individual editions before the 1623 Folio.
explanation.definitionFit: Early printed texts of single Shakespeare plays were published in this format, folded sheets of four leaves.

clue.text: Small rodent consumes a loud poet

indicators.note: consumes means the rodent swallows the next pieces, taking them inside

parts.note: a cavy is a guinea pig
F is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: A little animal gobbling up a noisy versifier.
explanation.definitionFit: Constantine Cavafy was the Greek writer of verse from Alexandria.

clue.text: First letter to show direction in sacred river

indicators.note: in means the direction sits inside the river's name

parts.note: Alph is the sacred river of Coleridge's Kubla Khan
E is east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: An opening message pointing the way along a holy river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where Alph, the sacred river, ran' is from Coleridge's Kubla Khan.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the opening character of the Hebrew alphabet.

clue.text: Sort of vague event in the cinema

definitions.text: Sort of vague event in the cinema

parts.words: Sort of vague event in the cinema
parts.note: the French new wave of film-making of the late 1950s and 1960s, the vague in question

explanation.surface: Something hazy happening at the movies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vague' is French for wave, so this kind of vague is the new one in French film.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the French word for new, which qualifies the vague in the film movement's name.

clue.text: French law concerning flower

parts.note: loi is French for law
re means concerning

explanation.surface: French legislation about a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a crossword joke for a river, something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower is something that flows, a river, here the longest in France.

clue.text: It was easy for Spenser

parts.note: Spenser's archaic spelling of a word meaning not difficult

explanation.surface: Writing came easily to the poet Spenser.
explanation.walkthrough: Spenser used deliberately old spellings in The Faerie Queene.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an archaic form of eath, meaning not hard, used by Spenser.

clue.text: Cooper's flat canvas

parts.note: a novel by James Fenimore Cooper whose setting is a broad level grassland

explanation.surface: A painting of a flat landscape by an artist called Cooper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canvas' suggests a painting; here it is the scene of a novel, the fifth Leatherstocking tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Fenimore Cooper's 1827 novel is set on the flat grasslands of the American West.

clue.text: Bog standard plant of the Elysian fields

definitions.text: Bog standard plant of the Elysian fields

parts.words: Bog standard plant of the Elysian fields
parts.note: a lily of Greek myth that carpeted the meadows of the dead, with a marsh variety too

explanation.surface: An ordinary plant growing in paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bog standard' is British slang for ordinary, but here a bog variety of the plant exists.
explanation.definitionFit: This lily-like flower grew in the Elysian meadows of Greek myth; a bog species also grows in Britain.

clue.text: It may be crossed in love, we read in 3

definitions.text: It may be crossed in love, we read in 3

parts.words: It may be crossed in love, we read in 3
parts.note: a line from Sheridan's The Critic claims a shellfish may be unlucky in love

explanation.surface: A creature disappointed in romance, as a play reports.
explanation.walkthrough: In Sheridan's play (the answer to 3) Tilburina's line is 'An oyster may be crossed in love'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bivalve shellfish is the creature Sheridan's line claims may suffer a broken heart.
